skill.name: database-optimizer
skill.description: Expert database optimizer for performance tuning, query optimization, indexing, caching, scaling, migrations, and cloud database cost control.
skill.summary: Optimize database queries, indexes, caching, scaling, migrations, and monitoring across relational, NoSQL, and cloud platforms.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Slow queries and weak database design can increase latency, cost, and incident risk. This skill guides query tuning, indexing, caching, scaling, and monitoring across database platforms.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes execution plans, slow query patterns, and database bottlenecks.
Recommends indexing strategies for relational, NoSQL, and cloud databases.
Designs caching, partitioning, sharding, and read scaling approaches.
Plans zero-downtime migrations, schema changes, and rollback checks.
Suggests monitoring metrics, benchmarks, and regression tests.
Balances performance improvements with cost and maintainability.
limitations: It cannot inspect a live database unless the user provides metrics and query details.
Recommendations require testing in staging before production use.
It does not replace a database administrator for high-risk operational changes.
It may need platform-specific documentation for new managed database features.

use_cases.title: Resolve slow application queries
use_cases.description: Diagnose execution plans, N+1 patterns, and ORM behavior before changing code or indexes.

use_cases.title: Plan safer production tuning
use_cases.description: Prioritize index, statistics, pooling, and migration changes with validation steps and rollback criteria.

use_cases.title: Control cloud database cost
use_cases.description: Compare resource usage, scaling options, caching layers, and workload placement for managed database services.

prompt_templates.title: Review a slow query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this slow query and table context. Explain likely bottlenecks, safer indexes, and tests to run before production changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build an indexing plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an indexing strategy for these query patterns, write frequency, table sizes, and storage limits. Include trade-offs and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design caching and scaling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a database performance plan for this workload. Cover caching, read replicas, partitioning, monitoring, and rollback safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this zero-downtime migration plan for a large table. Identify lock risks, data backfill strategy, monitoring, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: A checkout query joins orders, customers, and payments and times out during peak traffic.
output: Likely bottleneck: joins scan high-volume tables without selective access paths.
First action: collect execution plan, row counts, existing indexes, and wait events.
Candidate fix: add a composite index aligned to filters and join keys, then benchmark in staging.

output_examples.input: A GraphQL API makes many user and order lookups for each page request.
output: Root cause: an N+1 access pattern creates repeated database round trips.
Recommended approach: batch related reads, add request-level loading, and cache stable reference data.
Validation: compare query counts, latency percentiles, and database CPU before and after.

output_examples.input: A SaaS team needs to move a large activity table without downtime.
output: Use a phased migration with dual writes or controlled backfill, depending on consistency needs.
Monitor locks, replication lag, write latency, and error rates during each phase.
Keep rollback criteria clear before switching reads to the new structure.

best_practices: Measure with real execution plans and production-like data before recommending changes.
Test each optimization independently so performance impact is attributable.
Document trade-offs, rollback steps, and monitoring thresholds for every production change.
anti_patterns: Adding indexes without matching them to actual query filters and sort patterns.
Optimizing schema design without measuring application access patterns.
Skipping benchmarks after changing queries, cache behavior, or database configuration.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers relational, NoSQL, cloud, time-series, graph, search, and columnar databases at a guidance level.

faq.question: Can it execute database changes?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis and recommendations. Users must run commands with proper review and permissions.

faq.question: What input gives the best results?
faq.answer: Provide schema details, query text, execution plans, table sizes, indexes, workload patterns, and latency goals.

faq.question: Does it help with cloud database cost?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare resource usage, scaling choices, caching, storage strategy, and managed service options.

faq.question: Can it diagnose N+1 problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review ORM, GraphQL, and service access patterns and suggest batching or eager loading options.

faq.question: Is it safe for production incidents?
faq.answer: Use it for structured guidance during incidents, but validate recommendations with database owners before making changes.
